answer: A meteg is printed. Most likely host: the aleph (א), with qamats, as in pausal אָֽתָּה. The mark sits nearer the right side of the tav, so a tav host cannot be ruled out.
visible_evidence: The whole word אתה is visible, including its lower points. Under the aleph there is a T-shaped qamats. The tav has a dagesh dot, and under it, left of center, is another T-shaped qamats. Between those two qamatses, under the right part of the tav, is a separate short vertical stroke with no crossbar. It is not part of either qamats and is not ink from the line below, so it reads as a meteg. Mark present: high certainty. Host: medium certainty. The aleph with qamats is the most likely host, because a meteg sits to the left of its host's vowel. But the stroke is printed under the tav's right half, which leaves the host letter unclear. The he has no point under it.
